abstract: Magnetic Fluid Hyperthermia is a cancer therapy that requires a uniform magnetic field to heat nanoparticles localized in the treatment volume. The efficacy of nanoparticles heating is studied using cells cultured in Petri dishes. The automated optimal design of the inductor to generate the magnetic field to heat nanoparticles in cells cultured in Petri dishes is presented, exploiting field analysis and a new version of an optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: Analytical modeling of a novel Vernier pseudo-direct-drive permanent-magnet machine
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The Vernier permanent-magnet machine (VPM) shares the same working principle as the MG-integrated machine with the main disadvantage being its low power factor. This paper proposes a novel Vernier pseudo-direct-drive machine (VPDD) combining the benefits of the VPM and the PDD. A 2-D subdomain analytical model is derived for a quick optimization of geometrical parameters. The analytical model is validated by the finite-element method. Compared with the VPM, the VPDD has a higher torque capability with a much smaller excitation current and a significantly higher power factor.

articleTitle: Novel analysis method on the vibration reduction for interior permanent magnet synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The main source of electromagnetic vibration are torque ripple, cogging torque and Magnetic Pull Force (MPF). However, the optimum design of torque ripple minimization actually doesn't have an effect on vibration. This paper carries out an investigation of electromagnetic vibration by using Finite Element Analysis (FEA). The validity of the proposed approach is confirmed by the results from the 2D FEA about relation of electromagnetic vibration and torque ripple. If the method is used, optimal design of low vibration and torque ripple is possible.

articleTitle: Simple L and T shaped butt joints composed of anisotropic and isotropic block cores in three-phase reactor
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a simple structure of L and T shaped butt joints composed of anisotropic and isotropic block cores is proposed. The iron loss of a three-phase reactor having the proposed joints is compared with that having ordinary joints composed of anisotropic block cores only. It is shown that the iron loss can be reduced by applying the proposed joints because the flux distribution becomes more uniform.

articleTitle: Nonlinear BEM-surface impedance boundary condition formulation for unstructured meshes
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Surface impedance boundary conditions are used to take into account electromagnetic phenomena in thin layers. By exploiting a dual geometrical discretisation of the surface of a conducting object, it can be used to formulate the skin effect as a circuit. The mesh can be either structured or unstructured as in case of triangular elements. The surface circuit can be coupled to a boundary element method for the region surrounding it giving rise to a hybrid solution. Field distribution along the depth of the conductor can account for nonlinearity if the analytical one dimensional solution is replaced by a numerical one. The hybrid technique is applied to the analysis of induction heating devices.

articleTitle: A temperature-dependent hysteresis model for soft ferrites based on a vectorial elemental operator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper introduces a temperature dependent hysteresis model based on a vectorial elemental operator with temperature-sensitive spontaneous magnetization and biaxial anisotropy for the soft ferrites. This model is validated by the substantial agreement between the simulated and measured major hysteresis loops of a soft ferrite sample at different temperatures.

articleTitle: Induction heating of adhesive for shoe manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper describes the induction heating of adhesive containing conductive fine particles for shoe assembly. The particles are heated on the principle of induction heating to increase the adhesive temperature. To do this, a 5kW induction heater is constructed and several experiments are conducted to design working coil. Finite Element Analysis is also conducted and the analytical and experimental results are compared to find optimal coil shape. From this study, we can develop a prototype of the induction heater for shoe manufacturing.

articleTitle: Topology optimization method for unsymmetrical rotor using cluster and cleaning procedure
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new topology optimization method that takes into account of unsymmetrical rotor structure. The phase angle of stator current needs not to be considered thanks of unsymmetrical rotor. Since the designed new unsymmetrical rotor develops only 6.3% lower output power with 38.3% less PM volume than those of Prius type generator, the effectiveness of the proposed method has been verified..

articleTitle: A stochastic method for characterization of soft magnetic material with a damped LC circuit
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a method to determine hysteresis parameters of an inductor's core with a closed magnetic circuit based on electric current and voltage curves of a damped LC circuit. The proposed procedure makes use of the concept of hysteresis modeling by separating the magnetic field into four components, which can be linearized in terms of its parameters. Thus, curves can be adjusted with a stochastic method in order to match experimental ones, allowing for determination of hysteresis parameters.

articleTitle: A new method for parameters obtaining of Jiles-Atherton hysteresis scalar model
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The here proposed method is based on rewriting the equations of Jiles-Atherton model to obtain a single non-linear ordinary differential equation used to identify the parameters. This equation involves only the interest variables: H, B with known values, and the model parameters with unknown values. The initial and anhysteretic magnetization curves, and filtering data are not used. The search space of the parameters is not restricted. The model parameters are readily obtainable. To validate the method, experimental data are compared with calculated data.

articleTitle: Topoprocessor: An efficient computational topology toolbox for h-oriented eddy current formulations
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: When solving eddy-current problems containing topologically non-trivial conductors with formulations using the magnetic scalar potential in the insulators, cohomology is recognized to be the only safe tool to obtain a well posed problem. This paper presents an efficient implementation of the recently introduced DS algorithm to compute the first lazy cohomology group generators of a tetrahedral mesh. The code will be available for download on request for non-profit use. Secondly, for the first time, the computational time required by the proposed toolbox for the topological pre-processing is compared with another freely available alternative on the same input mesh.

articleTitle: A new robust optimization approach applied to permanent magnet synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a new robust optimization algorithm is proposed. The new approach includes the concept of contour lines which share a local peak and uses the information of the contour areas. The validity was evaluated by mathematic function and applied to optimal design of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM).

articleTitle: 3D analysis of inspection method of opposite side defect in steel using AC square wave magnetic field with DC bias taking account of minor loop
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The alternating magnetic flux leakage testing is one of the electromagnetic non-destructive inspection method for detecting the surface defect on steel plate. By this inspection method, since the alternating magnetic field of high frequency is used, only the surface defect on the steel plate is detected. In this paper, the inspection method for the opposite side defect in the steel plate using the magnetizing current of AC square wave on DC bias by this inspection technique is proposed. The behavior of flux in steel is examined using 3-D nonlinear FEM taking account of minor loops and eddy current. It is shown that the inspection of opposite side defect in the steel plate is possible by using the impressed magnetic field AC square wave on DC bias.

Author Keywords: AC square wave on DC bias magnetic field

articleTitle: A gear efficiency improvement in magnetic gear by eddy-current loss reduction
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Magnetic gear has eddy current loss due to permanent magnets (PMs) unlike the mechanical gear. The eddy current loss becomes a main cause of decrease of gear efficiency. Therefore, this paper presented the eddy current loss reduction design of the PMs in the magnetic gear. The eddy current loss is calculated using a non-linear finite element method (FEM) based on 3-D numerical analysis and the effect of eddy current loss on the gear efficiency is analyzed.

articleTitle: Eddy current inspection of a ferromagnetic material, effect of a biaxial stress state
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this work, the influence of mechanical stress in a ferromagnetic material on the signal provided by an inspecting eddy current probe is studied using a finite element modeling.

articleTitle: Full-wave correction of quasi-static models using finite element subproblems: Application to high frequency wound inductors
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Finite element subproblems are employed to provide full-wave corrections of quasi-static models of high frequency wound inductors. A particular attention is paid on the correction of the global voltage-current equation. The error made by the classical assumption which consists in decoupling the electric and magnetic fields is therefore accurately quantified at different frequencies, at the local (fields) and global (impedance) levels.

articleTitle: Design, modelling and optimization of a pseudo direct drive
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this digest, a pseudo repeat pattern approach is used to size a Pseudo Direct Drive (PDD) for wind power applications. Finite element analysis and optimization techniques are applied to improve the preliminary design of PDD.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a superconducting induction magnetic levitation device for hydraulic turbo-generator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To solve the problem caused by the heavily axial gravity load of the rotor and main shaft of the hydraulic generators, a superconducting induction magnetic levitation device is proposed for hydraulic generator system. AC superconducting windings are implemented to increase the levitation force. The basic structure and principle are introduced. According to the calculated magnetic field distribution, the AC loss power of the superconducting winding is estimated. In addition, the levitation force and torque are obtained and analyzed under different condition.

articleTitle: Heat source analysis of induction heater for electric vehicle
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The electric vehicle requires the device to separately generate a heat, because there is no engine. The induction heater is one of the devices to generate a heat. The induction heater is a method of heating the work piece indirectly by flowing an AC current to a coil. The case of induction heater uses the high frequency, and the skin effect is generated in the work piece. In this case, the calculation of the loss or power is difficult, because the range of the skin depth is different. In this paper, the induction heater is analyzed by co-simulation. And, the induction heater model and full bridge circuit are produced. Finally, the simulation values are verified through experiments.

articleTitle: EMI reduction of PMSM drive through matrix converter controlled with wide band gap switches
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: An innovative method in reducing the electromagnetic interference of electric machine drives has been proposed in this paper. In this method, matrix converter with wide band gap switches is used for controlling the permanent magnet synchronous machine drive. This control system not only make the controlling smooth but also have the capability to reduce the electromagnetic interference, since the switching frequency is controlled through the higher resolution technique. In this method, Finite element analysis of the PMSM is implemented and coupled with the Matlab Simulink simulation. In addition to the modeling, numerical simulation for two different wide band gap switch i.e. Silicon (Si) IGBT and Silicon Carbide (SiC) MOSFET carried out and compared the results in simulation and experiment. The results of the proposed equivalent source models show that ripple in torque and speed response as well as harmonics in stator current for SiC-MOSFET is less than Si-IGBT. The electromagnetic implication of this study is that with the proposed equivalent model, the radiated and conducted electromagnetic interference are reduced.

articleTitle: Parametric analysis of magnetoharmonic problem based on proper generalized decomposition
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Parametric problems have been successfully studied with the Proper Generalized Decomposition (PGD) in engineering. In this communication, the PGD approach is applied to build a surrogate model of a parametric magnetoharmonic problem. With the proposed example, the solution is parameterized with four variables (position, angular frequency and electrical conductivity of two subdomains).

articleTitle: Variable preconditioned Krylov subspace method with communication avoiding technique for electromagnetic analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The Variable Preconditioned (VP) Krylov subspace method with communication avoiding (CA) technique is adopted for the solver of a linear system obtained from electromagnetic analysis, and the numerical features are investigated. A massive communication time between processing units or GPU/MIC is the problem for parallelization efficiency that needs to be solved. Although κ-skip Krylov subspace method is one of a settlement for the problem, convergence property of the method is becoming worse. From this reason, we adopt κ-skip Krylov subspace method as inner-loop solver of the VP Krylov subspace method. The result of computation shows that the VP Krylov subspace method with CA technique is very effective for the linear system obtained from electromagnetic analysis.

articleTitle: Modelling of magnetic properties in soft magnetic composite material under rotational magnetization
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a vectorial magnetic hysteresis model based on a vectorial elemental operator and its distribution function to represent the magnetization mechanisms of soft magnetic materials. The magnetic hysteresis of a soft magnetic composite material under rotational magnetization is simulated and compared with the experimental results.

articleTitle: Interactive toolbox for the visualization of typical antenna attributes
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To understand wave propagation phenomena complex mathematical and physical theory is needed. Therefore, many undergraduate students find it very difficult to deal with this area of research. In the present paper an interactive toolbox is proposed which can help students to gain profounder knowledge and understanding of wave propagation effects.

articleTitle: Improved parabolic equation method for narrow-band loran-C ASF prediction over irregular terrain
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: We previously introduced the parabolic equation (PE) method, based on the split-step Fourier-transform (SSFT) algorithm, to efficiently predict Loran-C additional secondary factor (ASF) over irregular terrain. The main disadvantage of this method, however, is that it cannot be used to model the actual time-domain (TD) modulated Gaussian pulse signal propagation due to the nature of the frequency-domain (FD) method itself. To overcome this drawback, an improved approach, based on the PE method, is employed to model the actual Loran-C ASF prediction. The main idea of this approach is that the forward and inverse discrete Fourier transform (DFT) techniques convert the TD wave propagation problem into a series of FD wave propagation problems that can be solved by the employment of the traditional PE method. The accuracy of the improved approach is demonstrated by numerical examples.

articleTitle: Proposal on a new type of second order edge elements in magnetostatic field analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A new type of second order edge element in magnetostatic field analysis is introduced. The two variables along the side edges of each element are merged into one variable, hence, the computational time can be reduced compared to conventional elements. Moreover, the accuracy of the results is identical to one using conventional second order elements.

articleTitle: Analytical modeling of manufacturing imperfections in double rotor axial flux PM machines: Effects on back EMF
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a general analytical model is proposed to investigate various eccentricities in double rotor axial flux permanent magnet (DRAFPM) machine, the back electromotive forces (EMFs) is calculated and compared in this paper. At first, the radial and tangential flux density in the air gap under healthy condition is developed via Maxwell's equations and Schwarz-Christoffel mapping. After that, variable air gap length and radii are introduced to calculate the flux density caused by eccentricities. The back EMF at each case is calculated and compared with that in healthy condition. At each section, FEM models are built to validate the analytical model, and the results show that the analytical model predictions agree well with those from the FE results. Finally, the analytical model is verified via experimental results.

Author Keywords: double rotor axial flux PM machine

articleTitle: A study on fault-tolerant operation of a two-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor based on structual alteration
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The paper proposes a fault-tolerant control strategy for a two-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) by a structural alteration. Firstly, a two-phase PMSM is designed with a structure of combination with two conventional single-phase U-core PMSMs. Each has a self-start ability because of the step air gap design on the inner side of stator, and two sets of magnet in the motor are placed as 90 electrical angle shift. If one is fault, the other can work continually. Secondly, a drive with the space vector modulation (SVM) technique is designed for the proposed system. Considering the possible faults, a fault-tolerant technique is proposed to improve the system robustness. The experimental results show the validity of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Sierpinski carpet fractal microstrip arrays for energy harvesting applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this work we introduce two fractal microstrip antenna arrays to be used in energy harvesting applications. These arrays were optimized in order to get impedance matching, reduced return losses, high gain and bandwidth. Then, energy harvesting simulations were performed using CST® and the efficiency results for both antennas are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Dot sensitivity analysis for topology optimization of dielectric material in electrostatic system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a dot sensitivity analysis for topology optimization of dielectric material in the electrostatic system. A dot sensitivity formula derived as a closed form is coupled to the level set method. Since the dot sensitivity analysis can generate a new material in a vacant region, it does not only require the initial design of the material, but also can generate diverse topologies. Numerical models are tested to show the usefulness of the dot sensitivity analysis.

articleTitle: A particle swarm optimization method applied to global optimization of inverse problem
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is a global optimal algorithm based on swarm intelligence. PSO is more popular due to its easiness in implementation and fast convergence speed. However, PSO will be trapped into local optima while it is used to solve complex, multimodal inverse problems. To establish a proper balance between the exploration and exploitation searches, this paper introduces a dynamic and adaptive mechanism for the three basic parameters. To preserve the diversity of the swarm, a particular best particle, which takes part in a mutation operation, is introduced in the modified PSO. The numerical results on a case study show that the proposed PSO finds the best results as compared to other ones.

articleTitle: A fast methodology for topology optimizations of electromagnetic devices
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To alleviate the excessive computational burden on topology optimizations, an efficient methodology on topology optimization is proposed. In the proposed methodology, a multi-scale ON/OFF method is designed to avoid using infinite number of decision parameters; and a stochastic approximation method is employed to minimize the computational costs when computing the sensitivity information. Numerical results are reported to showcase the merits of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Determination of winding lumped parameter equivalent circuit by means of finite element method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, finite element method is used in order to determine electrical parameters of a machine winding lumped element model. This model allows to study the distribution of the turn-to-turn maximum voltage stress. The suitability of the method is validated by comparison with measurements.

articleTitle: Wireless power transfer for electric vehicle using an adaptive robot
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Charging time and power transfer efficiency are the main issues of wireless power transfer for electric vehicle. It is proposed in this paper to resolve both of the issues using the concept of transformer induction. An autonomous robot arm equipped with several sensors is mounted to the vehicles undercarriage to carry the receiving coil and locate it at the right place which is into the transmitting core during charge. In addition, silicon carbide MOSFETS are used in power converter to keep the frequency as high as possible to decrease the charging time. Through this method, the above issues and the problem of large non permeable air gap and accordingly electromagnetic interference are resolved. Also the charging time is decreased dramatically.

articleTitle: Validation of numerical models of portable wireless devices for near-field simulation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The near-field validation of the numerical models of portable wireless devices is becoming indispensable, especially, when checking SAR (specific absorption rate) compliance for regulatory limits by computer simulation. The current practice for such validation is to compare measured and simulated electromagnetic fields in a standard flat phantom. This paper proves that a cheaper and faster technique based on comparing measured and computed one-port characteristics of the antennas can equivalently accomplish the validation. The proof is based on the reciprocity theory and high-order Born approximation. The equivalence of the standard and new validation techniques is illustrated by comparing measurements and computations.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of steady state of magnetostatic problems coupled with nonlinear electric circuit
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this communication, the Waveform Relaxation-Newton Method with time periodic condition is used to model magnetostatic problems coupled with nonlinear electric circuit equations. The aim is to impose directly the steady state. As example of application a 3-phase transformer connected to a 6-pulse diode rectifier with RL load is studied.

Author Keywords: Nonlinear magnetostatic problem coupled with nonlinear electric circuit equation

articleTitle: Numerical model for quench calculations in a 10 kA MgB2 superconducting cable
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Multi-filamentary MgB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> superconductors are well suited for high power applications, especially, for the creation of high current DC compact cables. In this framework, a 10 kA all superconducting cable with a diameter of 60 mm is under development inside the European project Best-Path. This cable working with MgB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> superconductors at 20 K will be cooled down with gaseous Helium at 20 bars. To investigate the protection of the cable in the case of fault current, lighting, or defects in conductors, a multi-physical numerical model has been developed.

articleTitle: Multi-simplex algorithm applied to FEM based optimal design of electric machine
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel global search optimization algorithm, Multi-Simplex Algorithm (MSA), is proposed. The MSA is the stochastic algorithm that utilizes the reflection operator of Simplex Method with scattered particles. Its effectiveness has been verified by applied on optimal design of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (IPMSM) aiming for reduction of Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) in its Back-EMF.

articleTitle: History based learning artificial bee colony algorithm for electromagnetic inverse problems
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) inverse problems are usually modeled as simulation-based optimization problems with multimodal and non-differentiable properties. These properties justify the invention of more effective optimization algorithms. Artificial bee colony (ABC) has already been applied to tackle EM inverse problems. This paper applies a tree structure to record all search moves of ABC. A history based learning ABC is proposed to assist the finding of promising search directions. Novel variation formula is invented to guide the move of honey bees. The proposed algorithm is applied to tackle a loudspeaker design problem. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is more effective and reliable than the compared algorithms.

articleTitle: Electrical conductivity tensor modelling of stratified woven-fabric carbon fiber reinforced polymer composite materials
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a new multi-scale approach to predict the effective electrical conductivity tensor of a woven-fabric composite layer is presented. The result is then used to model the behaviour of a stratified composite material composed by a pileup of woven-fabric layers with different relative orientations. To take into account the orientation and the anisotropy of the material a 3D multilayer hexahedral degenerated elements method is used to model the anisotropic plate. This approach enables to take account random distribution of carbon fibers in the yarns, 3D effects and electric percolation threshold with an acceptable numerical cost. The developed model is then validated by experimental results.

articleTitle: Homogenization method for laminated iron core taking account of hysteretic property
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a homogenization method for laminated iron core taking account of hysteretic property by using the isotropic vector play model. Furthermore, we apply the proposed homogenization method to finite element magnetic field analyses to demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Method for current/voltage post-correction for efficient hysteretic magnetic field analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Two post-processing methods of correcting the current-voltage property are proposed for the efficient hysteretic magnetic field analysis. One uses the instantaneous power difference by the post-processing method. The other gives an equivalent resistance to the hysteresis effect. The analysis of the drum-type ferrite-core inductor using the former method agrees with the finite element magnetic field analysis that directly handles the hysteretic property.

articleTitle: Analytical modeling and experimental verification of vehicle horn considering skin effect using coupled electric and magnetic circuits
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents an analytical modeling of an axisymmetric vehicle horn considering skin effect in solid cores based on coupled electric and magnetic circuits. The vehicle horns usually use the solid cores for mass production and cost reduction, but such cores induce high eddy current loss and low inductance. That makes it difficult to estimate the performances of the vehicle horn because of high iron loss current. Thus, the coupled circuits reflect the skin effect of the electromagnetic waves, which travel in conducting mediums under a time-varying field, as well as the nonlinear magnetization curves. The concept “coupled” is introduced to determine the magnetic flux and the back electro-motive force through analyzing the effective current in the electric circuit and the system reluctance in the magnetic circuit. In addition, the analytical approaches to equivalent iron loss resistance and inductance are also presented. Finally, the prototype is tested to validate the aforementioned method.

articleTitle: Incorporating light beam search in a vector normal boundary intersection method for multiobjective inverse problem
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To combine the preferences of a decision maker in the evolution process of a vector optimizer in finding an arbitrary fraction of the Pareto front of a multiobjective problem, the light beam search method is proposed to be incorporated into a vector normal boundary intersection method. To adapt different preferences, a new transformed projection mechanism is introduced; to enhance the diversity of the algorithm, a dynamic transitional sub-domain strategy is used. Typical mathematical functions and practical inverse problems are used to testify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multiharmonic resolution of nonlinearly coupled electrovibromechanical systems using domain decomposition
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper compares linearly as well as nonlinearly preconditionned domain decomposition methods for nonlinear, coupled electrovibromechanical problems. The iteration unknowns for the domain decomposition are either taken only at the subdomain interfaces or in the whole volume. Both staggered and monolithic electrostatic/elastic/acoustic formulations are considered for the multiphysics problem. Because of the nonlinearity a pure harmonic excitation leads to multiple harmonics in the displacement field, in the pressure field and in the electric potential. A novel multiharmonic resolution method is used to automatically generate the required multiharmonic formulations and thus avoid the need of time-stepping to reach steady state.

articleTitle: Ionospheric time-delay of satellite signal propagation calculation based on FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: To improve the accuracy of satellite signal propagation, we designed a moving-window finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, in which the distribution of the electron density given in IRI-2007 model was used, and calculated the time-delay for a uniform distribution of the electron density to prove the validity, the calculated result fitted the theoretical result. So it is proved our FDTD method is reliable. Then three different electron distributions with the same integral results (TEC) were calculated by our method and it can show the difference of the time-delay under different conditions. These results above can be used to assess existing models and the theory basis for an improved satellite signal propagation model.

articleTitle: A novel double-rotor parallel hybrid-excitation machine for electric vehicle propulsion
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A novel double-rotor parallel hybrid excitation machine with improved field adjustment capability is proposed in this paper. The key is to embed a stator electrical-excitation machine (SEEM) into the internal space of permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) and the problem of magnetic field adjustment for conventional PMSM is effectively solved. This design integrates the merits of PMSM and SEEM, and provides high power density and a wide constant power speed range, thus making the proposed machine especially suitable for electric vehicle propulsion. In this paper, the selection, combination and design consideration for effective integration are investigated and verified by finite-element analysis.

articleTitle: Modelling the effect of multiaxial stress on magnetic hysteresis of electrical steel sheets: A comparison
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A simplified multiscale approach and a Helmholtz energy based approach for modelling the multiaxial stress dependent magnetic hysteresis behavior of electrical steel sheets are compared. The models are identified from uniaxial magneto-mechanical measurements. Both approaches model the hysteresis losses under multiaxial stresses with reasonable accuracy compared to the measurements.

articleTitle: Fast variable preconditioned conjugate gradient method using deflation technique
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Fast Linear solvers for electromagnetic field analysis on parallel computing environments are discussed. The preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) using incomplete Cholesky (IC) decomposition has been used for finite element analysis so far. However, the IC preconditioning is not suited to parallel computing due to forward/backward substitutions. For this reason, a variable preconditioning in which iterative solvers such as CG are used for preconditioner is introduced in this paper. This method is fit for recent computers with multi core CPUs because of high parallelizing efficiency. Moreover a deflation technique which replaces small eigenvalues with zeros in the system matrix is introduced so as to improve the convergence of PCG method. Numerical results show that the proposed method has high parallelizing efficiency as well as good convergence property in comparison with the conventional PCG method.

articleTitle: An improved quantum particle swarm optimization applied to inverse problem in electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The development of global optimal techniques for inverse problems in electromagnetics has been successful in the last few years. However, inspired from the classical Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm and quantum mechanics, this work presents an improved Quantum based particle swarm optimization (QPSO) by using a tournament selection strategy. Also, a new index, called Tbest (tournament best), is incorporated into the QPSO to further enhance its performance. The feasibility and merit of the proposed approach are verified by mathematic functions and an electromagnetic inverse problem.

articleTitle: Improved Quasi-3D finite element method for an axial flux permanent magnet motor
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In the quasi-3D FEM, the overall performance of axial flux permanent magnet (AFPM) motor can be obtained by assembling 2-D FEM results of each cross section along a radial direction. A critical drawback of quasi-3D FEM is its inability to conduct finite element (FE) analysis when rotor back-iron and permanent magnet (PM) have different length along radial direction. In order words, because there is no PM in computation region of quasi-3D FEM when rotor-back iron is longer than PM along lamination direction, FE analysis cannot be done. To address this problem, we propose an improved quasi-3D FEM which considers AFPM motor with different length between rotor-back iron and PM. From results of the 3D FE analysis, the validity of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Determination of flux tube portions by adjunction of electric or magnetic multivalued equipotential lines
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In 2D electrostatic and magnetostatic finite element problems, portions of flux tubes are defined by field lines together with their orthogonal lines. These two sets of lines can be obtained as the isovalue lines of scalar and vector potentials. One set is related to a multivalued potential that, when made single-valued via the definition of cuts, undergoes discontinuities, resulting in lines interruptions at the cuts. A method is proposed for obtaining continuous isovalue lines for the multivalued potentials. This then helps in locating selected portions of flux tubes and quantifying their equivalent properties, i.e., capacitances or reluctances, to be used in equivalent circuits.

articleTitle: Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain method for 3D modeling of ground penetrating radar scenarios
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain (DGTD) method is used to model full Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) scenarios. The bi-static GPR is made of two identical Vivaldi antennas, which are accurately modeled in front of a sand box in order to detect and localize some buried objects. Our approach is validated by comparison with either synthetic data provided by CST-MWS or experimental data acquired in a controlled laboratory experiment in an anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Dynamic reluctance mesh modeling and losses evaluation of permanent magnet traction motor
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Dynamic reluctance mesh method (DRM) combines the advantages of finite-element method(FEM) and magnetic equivalent circuit method. The attractive advantages of this method include as follows: less mesh units compared with FEM; higher computational accuracy than traditional magnetic equivalent circuit method. This paper presents modeling and analysis of permanent magnet synchronous motor using DRM. Furthermore, the iron losses are investigated. The FEM results are presented to validate the model.

articleTitle: Iron loss of electrical steel considering rotational magnetization and laminated direction mechanical stress
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of laminated direction mechanical stress on the magnetic properties of electrical steel sheets. A 2D measuring system has been developed. The vectors B and H in electrical steel are measured under alternating and rotational magnetization, when different stress is exerted. Based on measuring results, iron losses are calculated.

articleTitle: Optimal force ripple design of mutually coupled linear switched reluctance machines with transverse flux by Taguchi method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents an optimization algorithm of Taguchi method for electromagnetic force ripple of mutually coupled linear switched reluctance machine with transverse flux, in which the force ripple is reduced from 49% to 31% and the average force improved significantly. The numerical results are in good agreements with finite elements analysis.

articleTitle: Electrical field evaluation around slender conductors by collocation boundary element method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Evaluation of surface electric fields, which is well described by Poisson equation, is of great importance on many occasions in power system. This paper proposes a boundary element method for long slender conductors. Examples show the method is convergent and shows great potential for the evaluation of electric field generated by slender conductors.

articleTitle: Post-processing magnetic measurement data of accelerator magnets by the boundary element method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The paper deals with the application of the boundary element method to the post-processing of magnetic measurement data in normal-conducting accelerator magnets.

articleTitle: Fast three-dimensional analysis of eddy currents in Litz wire using integral equation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Eddy current loss in a Litz wire which has three-dimensional structure is analyzed using integral equation method considering proximity effect. In the present method, one-dimensional integral equation is formulated for the perpendicular component of the complex magnetization vector generated by eddy currents in the wire. It can effectively be solved by iterative methods to compute the eddy currents due to proximity effect.

articleTitle: Design and realization of a current sensor for impulse current waveform measurement
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a current sensor for current measurement in high frequency high voltage pulse power supplies, the output of which is DC current superposed with impulse current waveform. The current sensor is made of two magnetic cores. One works in fluxgate principle to measure DC current. While the other is based on transformer effects for impulse current measurement. The impulse current sensor has a wide bandwidth up to 340kHz. It can measure DC with an accuracy of about 30/00, and the measurement errors for impulse current peak is limited to 6%.

articleTitle: Fast identification problems in 3D iron core fusion devices
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In nuclear fusion devices, unknown currents modelling the plasma behavior have to be estimated within the strict instability growth time, because of both control and stabilization requirements. Nowadays, suitable identification procedures mainly based on information coming from the magnetic measurements are available, typically in the axisymmetric frame. The presence of iron materials strongly increases the complexity for the lack of both linear behavior and 2D hypothesis. The paper proposes and compares two effective iron modeling and assesses their suitability for practical applications.

articleTitle: Model reduction & manifold learning — Based parametric computational electromagnetism: Fundamentals & applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Techniques based on the use of separated representations, are at the heart of the so-called Proper Generalized Decomposition methods. Such separated representations were employed for solving multidimensional models suffering the so-called curse of dimensionality, transient models within a non-incremental integration schema and in the context of uncertainty propagation. Then, its use was extended for separating space coordinates making possible the solution of models defined in degenerated domains, e.g. plate, shells or laminates, and finally for addressing parametric models where model parameters were considered as problem extra-coordinates.

articleTitle: Torque ripple minimization for interior PMSM with consideration of magnetic saturation incorporating on-line parameter identification
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A novel torque ripple minimization approach for interior permanent magnet synchronous machine (IPMSM) considering magnetic saturation is proposed in this digest. The inductance variations due to magnetic saturation have a great influence on the torque ripple minimization for IPMSMs. Thus, a voltage injection based on-line parameter identification scheme is proposed to estimate the dq-axis inductances, which are then incorporated in the optimal current design to improve the torque ripple minimization performance. Experimental tests are conducted on an IPMSM to validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Processing of a carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminate part by microwaves
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Microwave (MW) technology relies on volumetric heating. Thermal energy is transferred through electromagnetic fields to materials that can absorb it at specific frequencies. The principal objective of this work is to model and simulate the interactions of the MW field with a composite laminated part, consisting of a stack of layers of different orientations, each layer made of resin matrix and carbon fibers.

articleTitle: Flux barrier effect of spoke-array magnets in flux-modulation machines
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Spoke-array magnet topology is capable of increasing the torque density of PM machines due to its flux focusing effect. However, a so-called flux barrier effect is found when this magnet topology is applied in flux modulation machines, which may offset the advantage in torque capability. From the view of flux distribution, the flux barrier effect is visually explained in this paper. Through numerical FEA, considerable reduction in main flux and output torque is verified.

articleTitle: Multi-objective design optimization of primary core in induction heating roll by level-set method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper deals with the multi-objective design optimization of the primary core in induction heating roll in consideration of heating performance, cost, and manufacturability. We effectively carry out the shape optimization of the core by combining the 2D level-set method with the 3D finite element method for the coupled nonlinear magnetic-thermal analysis.

articleTitle: 3D volume integral formulation based on facet elements for the computation of AC losses in superconductors
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A 3D volume integral formulation based on a generalization of the PEEC method (Partial Element Equivalent Circuit) for the computation of AC losses in the superconducting materials is developed and detailed. This can be achieved by the use of finite element facet interpolation for the current density. Several strengths appear with this approach. The method which is both light (we don't require to mesh the air) and precise, ensures highly the conservation of current and therefore leaves hope for a good performance in solving highly nonlinear problems.

articleTitle: A novel iron loss calculation algorithm using vector play model taking account of the rotating magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new iron loss calculation algorithm taking rotating magnetic fields into account by incorporating a vector stop model and one-dimensional finite element analysis of eddy current distribution. The algorithm is applied to a non-oriented material 35PN440, and its results are compared with conventional and the measured ones.

articleTitle: Loss and air-gap force analysis of cage induction motors with non-skewed asymmetrical rotor bars based on FEM
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Non-skewed rotors can be used to eliminate the slot harmonic field, as well as, the noise and vibration can also be weakened effectively. However, it is difficult to determine the spatial distribution of the asymmetrical rotor bars and slot combinations, which can affect the loss and air-gap force significantly. Taking a 5.5kW, 4-pole induction motor as an example, this paper studies the influence of the above factors on the loss and air-gap force systematically, by using Finite Element Method (FEM), and the experiment validation on efficiency and no-load noise are also performed on a 5.5 kW prototype.

articleTitle: Computation of magnetic forces using degenerated airgap element
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient method to calculate the magnetic forces on bodies in contact. The forces are computed through local application of the virtual work principle on degenerated airgap elements. These results are compared with those from different models and validated with measurements on a permanent magnet setup. Not only is this technique very accurate, but also reduces the computational burden related to the problematic meshing of thin layers.

articleTitle: A computer aided education system based on augmented reality by immersion to 3-D magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this paper, a visualization system of immersion into 3D magnetic field based on the augmented reality technology using a head mounted display, for education purpose, is presented. By utilizing the proposed visualization method, a user can easily observe and perceive in real-time a magnetic field distribution generated by single/multiple sources (e.g., permanent magnets and/or coils) and other magnetic/nonmagnetic material in an augmented 3-D space.

articleTitle: 2D finite element model reduction for copper losses calculation in switched reluctance machines
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This article proposes a 2D finite element model reduction that profits from one finite element solution of the machine modeling to find fast solutions in slots sub-domains when any variation of geometrical data occurred. It provides clear advantages in repetitive analyses when we search the optimized winding configuration for a given number of turns.

articleTitle: Eddy current characterization using robust meta-heuristic algorithms for LS-SVM hyper-parameters optimization
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents the use of the Least Square Support Vector Machines (LS-SVM) technique, combined with the Finite Element Method (FEM), to characterize small cracks in order to get a fast non-destructive inspection. The LS-SVM is a statistical learning method that has good generalization capability and learning performance. LS-SVM trained model is proposed to predict crack sizing using experimental signals acquired from an Eddy Current (EC) sensor. The FEM is used to create the data set required to train this model. The performance of LS-SVM model depends on a careful setting of its associated hyper-parameters. Different tuning techniques for optimizing the LS-SVM hyper-parameters are studied: Electromagnetism-Like Mechanism (EM), Opposition Based Electromagnetism-Like Mechanism (OBEM) and Teaching Learning Based Optimization (TLBO). Results show that TLBO algorithm provides a good compromise between accuracy and computational cost.

articleTitle: Power balance approach to study electromagnetic damping in rotor dynamics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The electromagnetic damping of mechanical vibrations in a cage induction machine with an eccentric rotor is studied. The method used in the study is based on the numerical power balance of the machine. Time-stepping finite element method is used to compute the powers. The damping power calculated from the power balance is used in the mechanical rotor model and the response of the system is observed.

articleTitle: A simple equivalent circuit model for shielding analysis of magnetic sheets
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a simple equivalent circuit model for estimating shielding performance of thin and flexible magnetic sheets, which are commonly used in modern mobile devices such as smartphones. The proposed equivalent circuit model can accurately represent the measurement setup using a microstrip line and a loop probe that are typically employed to evaluate a shielding effectiveness (SE) of commercial magnetic absorbing sheets. The calculated SEs using the proposed model are validated by full-wave simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Transient characteristics analysis of a 380V/30kVar superconducting controlled reactor
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This digest proposed a model of superconducting controllable reactor and calculates its reactance based on finite element method. In order to ensure the safe operation of superconducting reactor, the digest devises a control system for superconducting windings based on S7-200 PLC after analyzing the DC component and overvoltage of superconducting winding and puts forward an optimal control strategy. A 380V/30kVar SCR was fabricated for experiments and the experimental results show the correctness of this method and the feasibility of the control device.

articleTitle: Effects of flux modulation poles on the radial magnetic forces in permanent magnet vernier machines
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper studies the effects of the flux modulation poles (FMPs) on the radial magnetic forces in permanent magnet vernier (PMV) machines. The air-gap flux density distribution in the PMV machine is analyzed by using a combination of the finite element analysis and analytical methods. And then, the radial force density is calculated by Maxwell's stress method. At no-load condition, the permeance harmonics by FMPs generate various air-gap flux density harnmonics by interacting with the magneto-motive force (MMF) harmonics of the magnet. As a result, the low order harmonics of the radial force density which may induce significant vibration is caused in the PMV machine. Furthermore, the characteristics of the radial force density under the load condition will be investigated.

articleTitle: Wide-band modeling for dual-band coil of wireless power transfer system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Dual-band wireless power transfer (WPT) system will be one of the noticeable researches about WPT because of communication between the transmitting and receiving resonators. To realize dual bands, an extra compensation circuit (CSC) is inserted into the original WPT coil. In this paper, we establish wide-band model for dual-band WPT coil on the basis of vector fitting (VF) and partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) method. Prototypes of dual-band coils are manufactured, and impedance of the CSC is measured. Measured results are approximated by VF, which show good fitting results.

articleTitle: Radiated EMI simulation for high-power ultra-precision PMSM system driven by PWM converter
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The radiated electromagnetic interference (EMI) for a high-power ultra-precision permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) system driven by a pulse width modulation (PWM) converter is evaluated. The conducted EMI model of the drive system is pre-simulated to extract the excitation for the radiated model. The 3D simplified models for all the devices in the drive system, including converter, multi-core shielded cable and PMSM are established using time harmonic electromagnetic field (EMF) finite element method (FEM). Diverse scenarios are considered to evaluate the EMI on the control pairs in shielded cable and the control cabinet. The EMI mitigation strategies to improve the machining precision of the PMSM are proposed.

articleTitle: A new robust surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization algorithm for an IPMSM design
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: For a multi-objective optimization problem applied to the electric machine design, a new robust surrogate-assisted algorithm is proposed in this research. The proposed algorithm can find a robust and well-distributed Pareto front set rapidly and precisely for robust nondominated solutions by using a kriging surrogate model and an uncertainty consideration with worst case scenario. The outstanding performances of the proposed algorithm are verified by a test function. Furthermore, through the application of the optimal design process of the interior permanent magnet synchronous motor, the feasibility of this algorithm is verified.

articleTitle: PEEC-based multi-objective synthesis of non-uniformly spaced linear antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Linear antenna arrays consisting of dipole antennas find wide applications in wireless communication systems. Typically, arrangements with uniform spacing between the array elements are applied to gain highly directive radiation patterns. In the present paper an antenna array arrangement with non-uniformly spacing between the array elements is synthesized in the multi-objective sense. The optimization relies on the firefly algorithm and the PEEC method.

articleTitle: Temperature and electromagnetic force analysis of GIB plug-in connector with different contact status under short circuit fault
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Multi-physics coupled FEM model is developed for evaluating contact degradation of gas insulated bus (GIB) plug-in connector under short circuit current impact. Contact spring is assumed as elastic spring element and contact spot is simulated by contact bridge model. Thermal/mechanical characteristics of plug-in connector with typical assembly conditions (conductor insert depth/angle) under short circuit (SC) fault are analyzed.

articleTitle: Preconditioning of a low-frequency electric field integral equation formulation with circuit coupling using H-matrices
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper introduces a way to couple an external electrical circuit to a basic Electric Field Integral Equation (EFIE) formulation for low frequencies. The EFIE classically uses Loop interpolation functions that can be seen as circuit loops. We can take advantage of this in order to use a circuit approach to connect an external circuit and to solve multiply connected problems. We will propose an efficient preconditioning based on the H-matrices.

articleTitle: Modeling of selected 3D electroheat coupled problems with time-varying geometries
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Novel approach to modeling of 3D coupled electroheat problems with time-varying geometries is presented. Instead of time-expensive remeshing of the whole system in every time step it is used the initial mesh that takes into account the expected geometric changes. In the course of computations, its relevant elements are able to adaptively change their shapes and material parameters. The methodology is illustrated with an example of combined cladding.

articleTitle: Shape and topology optimization of electrical machines using lie derivative-based analytical sensitivity analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The paper addresses the optimal design of electric machines, through the general setting of both shape and topology optimization. The optimization problems are efficiently solved with a classical gradient-based mathematical programming algorithm. An analytical sensitivity analysis for the nonlinear magnetostatic problem that can handle both shape and topology design variables, based on the Lie derivative is derived and applied to the optimal design of an interior permanent magnet (IPM) machine.

articleTitle: Influence of varying bundle structures on power electronic systems simulated by a coupled approach of FEM and PEEC
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Even for litz wire conductors consisting of the same amount of strands, the frequency-dependent power losses on system level differ significantly between different bundle structures. The multi-scale problem consisting of electromagnetic effects in the dimension of microns which influences a power electronic system on macroscopic level has been examined by a coupled simulation approach based on the FEM and PEEC method. Common PEEC approaches have been adapted to highly complex litz wires by enhanced mathematical methods for sparse-matrices. The simulation results have been verified by measurements up to 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Fast global terminal sliding mode control method for torque regulation on disc coreless permanent magnet synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The disc coreless permanent magnet synchronous motor (DCPMSM) is drived by an inverter with current source chopper. A fast global terminal sliding mode control (FGTSMC) method is proposed in this paper for the torque loop, and the instantaneous torque is predicted. The proposed control system can dramatically reduce the current ripple of the DCPMSM by low inductance. The feasibility of this proposed control method is confirmed by simulation and experimental results.

Author Keywords: Disc coreless permanent magnet synchronous motor (DCPMSM)
fast global terminal sliding mode control (FGTSMC)

articleTitle: Design and control characteristics of guidance system for passive maglev transport system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Recent OLED display manufacturing process requires non-contact conveyor systems not generating particles to increase productivity. To avoid supplying power and heating in vacuum, a passive maglev transport system can be a promising solution because it has no actuators in moving carriers and all actuating electromagnets are installed on the ground. In this paper, we deal with the design and control characteristics of the guidance system for the passive maglev transport system. The proposed guidance system can generate bi-directional motion using one electromagnet and the guidance system is designed and analyzed in details using FEM tools. The guidance control characteristics were analyzed through impact tests using the manufactured passive maglev transport system.

articleTitle: A simplified method for acquisition of the parameters of Jiles-Atherton hysteresis scalar model without use of derivatives
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: Several methods have recently been proposed to identify the parameters of Jiles-Atherton model, e.g. differential evolution method, particle swarm optimization, and optimization branch and bound. In this work, it is presented a simplified method that avoids the rough calculation of derivatives, the rough calculation of integrals and avoids filtering data during the processing of the material characterization. Other advantages of proposed method are speed in the parameter calculation, the initial and anhysteretic magnetization curves and restrictions on the search space of parameters are not used, the search space of parameters is wide ranging from zero to infinity, it uses a trust region strategy to improve the robustness when the initial set of parameters is far from solution. In order to validate the method, simulated loops are compared with experimental ones.

articleTitle: Double-layer BEM for generic electrostatics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This contribution has two main goals. First one is to highlight the superiority of the DLA (Double-Layer Approach) contrary to the conventional IEM (Integral Equation Method) for the analysis of the electrostatic problems. The second goal is to point out to the very frequent incorrect modeling approaches when applying electro-static analysis for the simulation tasks in the dielectric design. Both targets are elaborated using the comparison with standard SCM (Surface Charge Method) on several examples from academic and industrial praxis.

articleTitle: Transfer torque performance comparison in coaxial magnetic gears with different flux-modulator shapes
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study effective flux-modulator shape in coaxial magnetic gear for transfer torque ripple mitigation. Using a non-linear finite element method (FEM) based on 2-D numerical analysis, the transfer torque performances of the magnetic gear with proposed flux-modulators are analyzed and quantitatively compared based on the same structure.

articleTitle: On-line evaluation of power transformer temperatures using magnetic and thermodynamics numerical modeling
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The power transformer heating should be monitored in order to avoid ageing of the insulation of impregnated paper and - consequently - the transformer's premature depreciation. This work describes the development and implementation of a thermal model aiming to calculate the internal temperatures in power transformers using numerical simulations to obtain an online model to estimate the hotspot temperatures. In order to validate the proposed procedure, a comparison with direct measurement in the power transformer is performed.

articleTitle: Research on a direct-drive wave energy converter using Outer-PM linear tubular generator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: An Outer-PM tubular linear generator has been designed to increase the power density and distance of relative movement. The design of the two buoys has been completed. Detailed design process of the proposed generator is described. Considering the cogging force and voltage, the linear generator has been optimized and final parameters have been determined. The integrated wave converter system has been manufactured and put into China's Yellow Sea based on the design results. The measured voltage is highly consistent with the simulation data. All the results show that the proposed generator is well suitable for wave energy conversion.

articleTitle: Inductance calculation method based on induced voltage
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for inductance calculation based on the relationship between current rate and induced voltage of conductor. Induced voltage is calculated by superposition of contribution of every magnetic flux element in space. This method can be applied to conductor segment and loop.

articleTitle: Surrogate-based MOEA/D for electric motor design with scarce function evaluations
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel surrogate assisted multi-objective evolutionary algorithm based on decomposition (s-MOEA/D) for the design of electric motors. The idea is to improve the surrogate gradually during the optimization. Simulation results show that the proposed method can outperform a regular multi-objective optimization algorithm with only a small portion of the computational cost.

articleTitle: Transient parameters calculation of salient-pole synchronous machine by finite element analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents a new method to calculate transient parameters of salient-pole synchronous machine by using finite element analysis(FEA). 2-D non-linear field-circuit coupled time-harmonic FEA analysis, static magnetic field FEA analysis and frozen permeability method are applied for transient equivalent circuit parameters calculation under no load three phases sudden short status. Transient parameters of the machine are obtained by definition formulas from equivalent circuit with the consideration of magnetic variation. Leakage inductances are particularly extracted and calculated. The transient parameters calculated by conventional method and experimental results of prototype machine are provided to confirm the accuracy of the presented method.

articleTitle: Effect of magnetic-valve distribution on reactance of magnetic controlled reactor
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The Multi-magnetic-valve structure is adopted in Magnetic Controlled Reactors (MCR) to reduce their current harmonics. However, the reactance can't be precisely calculated for its complicated structure. In this paper, an improved method to calculate its inductance is presented and the simulation analysis based on finite element method (FEM) verified its validity. The analysis results demonstrate that the length and the number of magnetic valves have a great impact on the inductance of MCR.

articleTitle: Extended TLM-2D numerical technique: An algorithm considering non-homogenous media and ionization
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents an extended TLM-2D numerical technique. Extensions include simultaneous consideration of non-homogenous media and ionization phenomena representation. Performance evaluation and representation of impulsive grounding systems embedded in concrete are considered as a study case. Analysis based on the Alternative Transients Program (ATP) and field measurements with different grounding systems configurations are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: An accurate vector Jiles-Atherton model for improving the FEM convergence
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper presents some modifications - compared to previous implementations - on the vector Jiles-Atherton (JA) model coupled with the Finite Element Method (FEM). The method is based on the 3D differential permeability formulation. A more precise calculation implies on the determination of the non-diagonal terms of tensor parameters. The main goal is to verify if such a change improves the convergence stability of the model coupled with FEM and if the use of the JA non-diagonal terms yields a more accurate hysteresis representation.

articleTitle: E-B eigenmode formulation for the analysis of lossy and evanescent modes in periodic structures and metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: We present an E-B linear eigenmode formulation for the analysis of periodic structures, including lossy periodic waveguides, photonic crystals and metamaterials. The proposed formulation does not exhibit spurious modes and can provide accurate complex-k dispersion diagrams for both propagating and evanescent modes, including those with oblique propagation.

articleTitle: A ferrofluid motion analysis with particle method and magnetic moment method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A ferrofluid under a magnetic field shows complex behavior. In this paper, a coupled analysis method is proposed employing the particle method and the magnetic moment method. The effectiveness of this method is verified when it is applied to the ferrofluid motion analysis.

articleTitle: Surface impedance boundary condition with circuit coupling for the 3D finite element modeling of wireless power transfer
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: A light 3D finite element magnetodynamic a-v model of resonant wireless power transfer coils using 3D surface impedance boundary condition strongly coupled with an external circuit is proposed, reflecting the importance of external circuit elements (notably capacitances) in the resonance phenomena. Preliminary results outline the accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: Low rotor eddy current losses SPM servo motors with fractional slot concentrated windings and novel retaining cage
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: This paper propose the stainless retaining cage of the FSCW-SPM servo motors for retaining the PM. Compared to the FSCW-SPM servo motors with normal stainless sleeve, there is low rotor eddy current losses by using the retaining cage. In this paper, the structure strength of the stainless retaining cage is analyzed and proven having the enough reliability.

articleTitle: Combined formulation for meshless-MoM hybrid method applied to 2D electromagnetic scattering
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: In this work a new formulation for the hybrid Meshless - Method of Moments is presented. The proposed approach employs the Interpolating Element Free Galerkin Meshless Method (IEFGM) and three different combinations of Electric Field Integral Equation (EFIE) and Magnetic Filed Integral Equation (MFIE). The technique is applied to solve the TMz scattering by an infinite dielectric cylinder and numerical and analytical results are compared.

articleTitle: The modified Jiles-Atherton model for the accurate prediction of iron losses
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The Jiles-Atherton (JA) model is a physics-based model which translates into a simple first order differential equation with five material constants known as the JA parameters. However, JA parameters identified from the saturated B-H loop cannot predict the inner loops accurately which poses a major hindrance for its use in the Finite Element (FE) based simulations. In this work, we have proposed a new approach which assumes one of the JA parameters to be a function of magnetic field intensity H or magnetic flux density B and requires the knowledge of inner loops. The improvement in the accuracy of the modified JA model has been demonstrated by comparing its predictions with the measurements and one of the already published works.

articleTitle: The influence of opening slots on stator surface-mounted permanent magnet machines
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: For stator surface-mounted permanent magnet (SSPM) machines, the two magnets mounted on the surface of one stator tooth are closely placed. In this paper SSPM machines with an opening slot placed between the two magnets on one stator tooth have been proposed. The influences of the opening slots on 6-stator-slot/8-rotor-pole (6/8) and 6-stator-slot/7-rotor-pole (6/7) SSPM machines which have equal stator slot areas and identical dosages of permanent magnets (PMs), are respectively investigated in terms of electromagnetic torques, cogging torques and torque ripples. And then, the predicted results are confirmed by finite-element analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: Influence of magnetic slot wedge on electromagnetic parameters and magnetic field distribution of turbo-generator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electromagnetic Field Computation (CEFC)
abstract: The working performance of an electric machinery can be improved by adopting magnetic slot wedge on the stator or rotor. To investigate the influence of the magnetic slot wedge on magnetic field distribution and the saturation reactance of a turbo-generator, a 2-D mathematical model for electromagnetic field of a 150MW air-cooled turbo-generator has been established by considering two different types of rotor slots. It is put forward that using weakly magnetic Cr-Ni alloy slot wedge and high-strength electric magnetic Fe-Cu alloy slot wedge to replace common A1 alloy slot wedge to improve the static stability performance of the generator.

articleTitle: Improvised asymptotic boundary conditions for quasi-static magnetic-field problems in ellipsoidal domains
